sections.title: The letter dê
paragraphs: The name of the letter is (dê) /de/. Its main sound is a consonant, heard in (dia) /ˈdi.ɐ/, which means day. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks the air. The letter has one sound.

sections.title: How to say dê
paragraphs: Touch the back of your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Block the air completely. Release the air forward with your voice on. Touch your throat to feel the buzz.

sections.title: Spelling rules for dê
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound. You hear it at the start of words, as in (dia) /ˈdi.ɐ/. You also hear it after other letters, as in (onde) /ˈõ.dɨ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with dê
paragraphs: Do not place your tongue behind your teeth on the gum, like in the English word day. Keep the tip firmly against the back of your upper teeth. Do not release a puff of air.
